title: Constructibility criterion on irreducible closed subsets of a Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] admitting a finite affine open cover by spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $E\subseteq |Y|$ be a subset. Suppose that for every irreducible closed subset $Z\subseteq |Y|$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], there is a nonempty relatively open subset $V\subseteq Z$ such that either $V\subseteq E$ or $V\cap E=\varnothing$. Then $E$ is constructible in $|Y|$ [def-weil-constructible-subset].

source.place: Tag 053Z (lemma-characterize-constructible-Noetherian), implication (2) to (1): a nonempty open disjoint from E is equivalent to E intersect Z not being dense in Z. The scheme specialization uses Properties Tag 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology) in literature/stacks-project/properties.tex.

proof.text: Put $X=|Y|$. The rings of sections of the given affine charts are their Noetherian chart rings by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus the assumed cover makes $Y$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Each of its finitely many affine charts is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Given any open covering of $X$, restrict it to each chart, choose a finite subcover there, and take the union of these finitely many finite subfamilies. Thus $Y$ is quasi-compact in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]: every nonempty family of closed subsets of $X$ has a minimal member. In particular a descending chain of closed subsets has a minimal term, and every later term equals that term. Hence $X$ is a Noetherian topological space.

source.place: Tags 01OV (definition-noetherian) and 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology); affine quasi-compactness: Algebra Tag 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact)

proof.text: Assume for contradiction that $E$ is not constructible in $X$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the family of closed subsets $C\subseteq X$ for which $E\cap C$ is not constructible in the ambient space $X$. This family is nonempty since $X\in\mathcal S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] choose an inclusion-minimal $C\in\mathcal S$. For every closed $D\subsetneq C$ in $X$, minimality says that $E\cap D$ is constructible in $X$. The empty set is constructible as the empty finite union in [def-weil-constructible-subset], so $C\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 053Z (lemma-characterize-constructible-Noetherian), converse, minimal bad closed subset

proof.text: The minimal bad subset $C$ is irreducible. Indeed, if it were reducible, [def-weil-irreducible-components] would give $C=C_1\cup C_2$ with each $C_i$ a proper relatively closed subset of $C$. Write $C_i=C\cap F_i$ with $F_i$ closed in $X$; thus both $C_i$ are closed in $X$. Step 2 makes both $E\cap C_i$ constructible in $X$. Closure under finite unions in [def-weil-constructible-subset] then makes $E\cap C=(E\cap C_1)\cup(E\cap C_2)$ constructible in $X$, a contradiction.

source.place: Tag 053Z (lemma-characterize-constructible-Noetherian), converse, reduction of the minimal bad closed subset to an irreducible one; using a binary closed decomposition

proof.text: Apply the hypothesis to the nonempty irreducible closed subset $C$ from Step 3. Choose a nonempty relatively open $V\subseteq C$ with $V\subseteq E$ or $V\cap E=\varnothing$. Write $V=C\cap O$ with $O$ open in $X$. Then $D=C\setminus V=C\cap(X\setminus O)$ is closed in $X$, and $D\subsetneq C$ because $V$ is nonempty. Step 2 implies that $E\cap D$ is constructible in $X$. Also $V=C\cap O$ is locally closed by [def-weil-locally-closed-subset], and hence constructible in the Noetherian space $X$ by the finite-union characterization in [def-weil-constructible-subset] (Tag 005L).

If $V\subseteq E$, the disjoint partition $C=V\cup D$ gives $E\cap C=V\cup(E\cap D)$, which is constructible by finite-union closure in [def-weil-constructible-subset] and Step 4. If $V\cap E=\varnothing$, the same partition gives $E\cap C=E\cap D$, which is constructible by Step 4. Both alternatives contradict $C\in\mathcal S$. Therefore $\mathcal S$ is empty and, taking $C=X$, the subset $E$ is constructible in $X=|Y|$.

source.place: Tag 053Z (lemma-characterize-constructible-Noetherian), converse, final contradictions in cases (a) and (b)
